summary: Project received owned sets incrementally and park live graph faults instead of replaying the entire store

replay.detail: Live receive/catch-up never falls back to full-store replay. Owned-set receipts, late member references and historical losing branches update only the affected ownership dependency closure. Explicit operator recovery, restore and existing migrations retain canonical replay.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes, payloads or storage versions change. The existing stale graph-health error_code stores projection-recovery-required/<static-reason>; its existing last-good position is preserved.

rules.detail: A non-contention incremental fault or unsupported guard rolls back the complete chunk and durably fences later automatic projection, including queued calls and restart. SQLite contention remains retryable. Blocked owned sets retain physical last-good desired/mission rows while withholding their effective selected view. Live base-history rebuilds preserve selection rows for every prefix owner, including overlaps; ownership checks and history folds use the same admitted prefix without consuming future descendants. No canonical replay semantics or checkpoint rules change.

compatibility.detail: GET /v1/health retains ready semantics and adds checks only while parked. The native $.value.checks row has id replication-projection-recovery-required, aggregate graph, nullable frontier, typed reason_code, read-time admitted current_target and phase projection. Doctor retains its existing check wire shape. Legacy bare recovery codes decode reason unknown; missing-health defaults do not fabricate a known frontier. Receipt still acknowledges durable delivery, not completed admission or projection.

downtime.detail: No new startup migration or replay. An existing parked state remains parked across restart.

manual.detail: A parked graph requires authorized explicit recovery, not repeated receive/restart retries. Doctor, the read-only health row, a single structured transition diagnostic and an existing operator operational-failure episode expose the reason and frontier.

recovery.detail: Successful explicit recovery clears the durable fence and the operator episode. Binary rollback needs no schema migration but restores the previous automatic full-replay fallback behavior; preserve the diagnostic and assess writer-hold risk before rollback.
